Theme 009 · Product UI as the stage

Form-Field Macro

Form controls shot like macro product photography: one gigantic input fills the frame with a crisp focus ring, a floating label and a caret as tall as a column, while neighbouring fields fall out of focus. The camera dollies from field to field; Acme Pulse is a switch you flip on, and the anomaly is a field that shakes red with the fix already suggested.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Floating-label input — the metric as a giant field; label sits in the border.
  • Focus ring — teal halo = attention; coral halo = anomaly.
  • Dropdown with depth of field — 38 options falling out of focus.
  • Macro toggle switch — turning Acme Pulse on is the reveal.
  • Inline validation — shake + helper text “since 09:42 · after deploy #2231”.
  • Segmented control / giant button — the human's choice, then the CTA.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Focus-ring morph — box-shadow spread 0→14 px plus a radius spring, 0.25 s, triggered on the kick.
  • Error shake — 5 px, 3 cycles, 0.3 s (fits inside one beat at 120 BPM), then the helper text types in at one word per 1/16.
  • Macro dolly + rack focus — camera glides between fields, 1.2 s sine.inOut, with 0→5 px blur on the neighbours; each arrival on a downbeat.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Why: form controls are universal and extremely legible at feed size; shooting them huge with product-photography light turns a boring UI into a tactile object, and “the field turns red with a suggested fix” is exactly how trustworthy validation feels. Risk: it can look like a UI-kit demo, so the macro camera, shallow focus and lighting must carry it.

Adapt to your product: pick the one field or setting that matters most in your product and shoot it huge; your agent is a switch the viewer watches being turned on.

References: Nielsen Norman Group — error messages in forms · Material 3 — text fields
